import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.DAGTransform

/-!
# NAND form of `DAGCircuit`s

A *NAND gate* of `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit` is the model's own `¬` gate read with at most two
arguments: `DAGGate.eval` evaluates a `¬` gate as the **negated conjunction** of its arguments
(`DAGGate.eval_eq`), so `⟨.not, [a, b]⟩` is `NAND(a, b)`, `⟨.not, [a]⟩` is `¬a = NAND(a)` and
`⟨.not, []⟩` is the constant `false`, the negation of the empty conjunction.  A circuit is in
*NAND form* when every gate is a NAND gate (`BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsNANDForm`).

The conversion `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toNANDForm` takes every circuit whose gates read at most
two vertices to NAND form.  It is an instance of the gate-rewriting host
`BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.rewrite` (`DAGTransform.lean`), with the gadget
`BoolCircuit.nandGadget`, built in the style of `BoolCircuit.deMorganGadget` (`DAGFanin.lean`):

| old gate | NAND gadget | gates | depth added |
|---|---|---|---|
| `∧[a, b]` | `t := NAND[a, b]`, `NAND[t]` | 2 | 2 |
| `∨[a, b]` | `NAND[a]`, `NAND[b]`, `NAND[¬a, ¬b]` | 3 | 2 |
| `∧[a]`, `∨[a]` | `NAND[a]`, `NAND[that]` | 2 | 2 |
| `∧[]` (true) | `f := NAND[]`, `NAND[f]` | 2 | 2 (absolute) |
| `∨[]` (false) | `NAND[]` | 1 | 1 (absolute) |
| `¬[…]` | copied | 1 | 1 |

Every gadget costs at most `fan-in + 2` gates and at most two levels, so the pass gives the
semantics, depth at most `2 · depth`, and at most `n + 4 · #gates` vertices.

**Disclosures.**
* NAND-form circuits are **not** `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsWellFormed`, which demands `¬` gates of
  fan-in exactly one; lemmas assuming well-formedness (`toTree_eval`, `deMorgan_*`,
  `binarize_*`) do not apply to them.
* The names avoid `NAnd`: `BoolCircuit.NAndCircuit` and `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.toNAnd`
  (`Basic.lean`) are the AND-rooted alternating normal form of the LMN development, not NAND
  gates.
* No ingested source states that `{NAND}` is a complete basis or gives a conversion; the
  conversion is glue, motivated by [BV14, Def 2.13, p008-b002] and [BV14, Thm 3.5, p014-b001]
  ("every Boolean NAND circuit").

## Main definitions

* `BoolCircuit.DAGGate.IsNAND` — a `¬` gate reading at most two vertices.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsNANDForm` — every gate is a NAND gate.
* `BoolCircuit.nandGadget` — the NAND gadget of the table above.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toNANDForm` — `C.rewrite (nandGadget n) nandGadget_correct hC`.

## Main results

All are statement-phase targets (glue):
* `BoolCircuit.DAGGate.eval_of_isNAND` (N1) — a NAND gate is the negated conjunction.
* `BoolCircuit.nandGadget_correct` (N2) — the gadget meets `GadgetCorrect` with depth factor 2.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toNANDForm_eval`, `toNANDForm_isNANDForm`, `toNANDForm_depth_le`,
  `toNANDForm_size_le` (N3–N6) — semantics, form, depth `≤ 2 · depth`, size `≤ n + 4 · #gates`.

While N2 is admitted, `sorryAx` reaches `toNANDForm` (whose body passes `nandGadget_correct` to
`rewrite`) and its consumers through N2 alone.

## References

* [BV14] Z. Brakerski, V. Vaikuntanathan, *Lattice-based FHE as secure as PKE*, ITCS 2014;
  ePrint 2013/541.
-/

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace BoolCircuit

variable {n : ℕ}

/-! ## NAND gates and NAND form -/

/-- A *NAND gate*: a `¬` gate (negated conjunction, `DAGGate.eval_eq`) reading at most two
vertices, `g.IsNAND ↔ g.kind = .not ∧ g.args.length ≤ 2`.  Fan-in 1 is negation and fan-in 0
the constant `false`.  Not `BoolCircuit.NAndCircuit` (`Basic.lean`, an AND-rooted normal form).
Glue; motivated by [BV14, Def 2.13, p008-b002; Thm 3.5, p014-b001]. -/
def DAGGate.IsNAND (g : DAGGate) : Prop := g.kind = .not ∧ g.args.length ≤ 2

/-- The NAND-gate predicate unfolded: `g.IsNAND ↔ g.kind = .not ∧ g.args.length ≤ 2`. -/
theorem DAGGate.isNAND_iff (g : DAGGate) : g.IsNAND ↔ g.kind = .not ∧ g.args.length ≤ 2 :=
  Iff.rfl

instance DAGGate.decidableIsNAND : DecidablePred DAGGate.IsNAND := fun g =>
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (g.kind = .not ∧ g.args.length ≤ 2))

/-- A circuit is in *NAND form* when every gate is a NAND gate:
`C.IsNANDForm ↔ ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.IsNAND`.  Such circuits are not `IsWellFormed`, which demands
fan-in-1 `¬` gates (disclosed).  Glue; motivated by [BV14, Def 2.13, p008-b002]. -/
def DAGCircuit.IsNANDForm (C : DAGCircuit n) : Prop := ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.IsNAND

/-- NAND form unfolded: `C.IsNANDForm ↔ ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.IsNAND`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.isNANDForm_iff (C : DAGCircuit n) :
    C.IsNANDForm ↔ ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.IsNAND :=
  Iff.rfl

instance DAGCircuit.decidableIsNANDForm (C : DAGCircuit n) : Decidable C.IsNANDForm :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.IsNAND))

/-- **N1. NAND semantics.** A NAND gate evaluates to the negated conjunction of the values it
reads: `g.IsNAND → g.eval vals = !(g.args.all fun a => vals.getD a false)`.  Glue (a reader of
`DAGGate.eval` on NAND gates).

**Proof sketch.** Rewrite with `DAGGate.eval_eq` (`DAGCircuit.lean`); the kind is `.not` by the
first component of `g.isNAND_iff`, so the match takes its `.not` branch. -/
theorem DAGGate.eval_of_isNAND {g : DAGGate} (hg : g.IsNAND) (vals : List Bool) :
    g.eval vals = !(g.args.all fun a => vals.getD a false) := by
  sorry

/-! ## The NAND gadget -/

/-- The NAND gadget, compiling the gate `g` after the gates `gs` (vertex `n + gs.length` is the
first new gate); it returns the new gate list and the vertex computing `g` (the table of the
module docstring):
* `¬[…]`: copied, `(gs ++ [g], n + |gs|)`;
* `∧[]`: `f := NAND[]`, `NAND[f]`; `∨[]`: `NAND[]`;
* `∧[a]`, `∨[a]`: `NAND[a]`, `NAND[that]`;
* `∧[a, b]`: `t := NAND[a, b]`, `NAND[t]`; `∨[a, b]`: `NAND[a]`, `NAND[b]`, `NAND[¬a, ¬b]`;
* an `∧`/`∨` gate of fan-in above two lies outside the gadget's domain (`nandGadget_correct`
  assumes fan-in `≤ 2`) and is copied.
Computable; glue, in the style of `deMorganGadget` (`DAGFanin.lean`). -/
def nandGadget (n : ℕ) (g : DAGGate) (gs : List DAGGate) : List DAGGate × ℕ :=
  match g.kind, g.args with
  | .not, _ => (gs ++ [g], n + gs.length)
  | .and, [] => (gs ++ [⟨.not, []⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)
  | .or, [] => (gs ++ [⟨.not, []⟩], n + gs.length)
  | .and, [a] => (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)
  | .or, [a] => (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)
  | .and, [a, b] => (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a, b]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)
  | .or, [a, b] =>
    (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [b]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length, n + gs.length + 1]⟩],
      n + gs.length + 2)
  | .and, _ :: _ :: _ :: _ => (gs ++ [g], n + gs.length)
  | .or, _ :: _ :: _ :: _ => (gs ++ [g], n + gs.length)

/-- The NAND gadget copies a `¬` gate:
`nandGadget n ⟨.not, args⟩ gs = (gs ++ [⟨.not, args⟩], n + gs.length)`. -/
theorem nandGadget_not (args : List ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨.not, args⟩ gs = (gs ++ [⟨.not, args⟩], n + gs.length) := by
  cases args with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons a l => rfl

/-- The NAND gadget on the constant `∧[]` (true):
`nandGadget n ⟨.and, []⟩ gs =
(gs ++ [⟨.not, []⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)`. -/
theorem nandGadget_and_nil (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨.and, []⟩ gs =
      (gs ++ [⟨.not, []⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1) := rfl

/-- The NAND gadget on the constant `∨[]` (false):
`nandGadget n ⟨.or, []⟩ gs = (gs ++ [⟨.not, []⟩], n + gs.length)`. -/
theorem nandGadget_or_nil (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨.or, []⟩ gs = (gs ++ [⟨.not, []⟩], n + gs.length) := rfl

/-- The NAND gadget on a fan-in-1 `∧` gate (double negation):
`nandGadget n ⟨.and, [a]⟩ gs =
(gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)`. -/
theorem nandGadget_and_singleton (a : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨.and, [a]⟩ gs =
      (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1) := rfl

/-- The NAND gadget on a fan-in-1 `∨` gate (double negation):
`nandGadget n ⟨.or, [a]⟩ gs =
(gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)`. -/
theorem nandGadget_or_singleton (a : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨.or, [a]⟩ gs =
      (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1) := rfl

/-- The NAND gadget on a fan-in-2 `∧` gate:
`nandGadget n ⟨.and, [a, b]⟩ gs =
(gs ++ [⟨.not, [a, b]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1)`. -/
theorem nandGadget_and_pair (a b : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨.and, [a, b]⟩ gs =
      (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a, b]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], n + gs.length + 1) := rfl

/-- The NAND gadget on a fan-in-2 `∨` gate (De Morgan):
`nandGadget n ⟨.or, [a, b]⟩ gs = (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [b]⟩,
⟨.not, [n + gs.length, n + gs.length + 1]⟩], n + gs.length + 2)`. -/
theorem nandGadget_or_pair (a b : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨.or, [a, b]⟩ gs =
      (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [b]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length, n + gs.length + 1]⟩],
        n + gs.length + 2) := rfl

/-- Outside its domain the NAND gadget copies the gate: for an `∧` or `∨` gate with at least
three arguments, `nandGadget n ⟨k, a :: b :: c :: l⟩ gs = (gs ++ [⟨k, a :: b :: c :: l⟩],
n + gs.length)` (`k ≠ .not`). -/
theorem nandGadget_of_three_le {k : GateKind} (hk : k ≠ .not) (a b c : ℕ) (l : List ℕ)
    (gs : List DAGGate) :
    nandGadget n ⟨k, a :: b :: c :: l⟩ gs = (gs ++ [⟨k, a :: b :: c :: l⟩], n + gs.length) := by
  cases k with
  | and => rfl
  | or => rfl
  | not => exact absurd rfl hk

/-- **N2. The NAND gadget is correct.** In the sense of `GadgetCorrect` (`DAGTransform.lean`),
with depth factor `2`, domain "fan-in at most two" and output predicate `DAGGate.IsNAND`:
`GadgetCorrect n 2 (fun _ l => l ≤ 2) DAGGate.IsNAND (nandGadget n)`.  That is, for every gate
`g` of fan-in at most two whose arguments are existing vertices of an acyclic gate list `gs`,
`nandGadget n g gs` only appends to `gs`, stays acyclic, returns a vertex below the new length
that computes `g`, adds at most `g.args.length + 2` gates and at most `2` levels over `g`'s
deepest argument, and every appended gate is a NAND gate.  Glue (the table of the module
docstring).

**Proof sketch.** As `deMorganGadget_correct` (`DAGFanin.lean`): case on the kind and on the
argument list (`nandGadget_not`, `nandGadget_and_nil`, …, the case readers above), and in each
case check the seven fields of `GadgetSpec`.  Extension and length are immediate (`ext` is the
emitted suffix; 1, 2 or 3 gates, at most `fan-in + 2`).  Acyclicity is `GatesAcyclic.snoc`
once per emitted gate (each reads only `g`'s arguments, below `n + |gs|`, or the gates just
emitted).  Values: `vertexValue_last` and `vertexValue_append` reduce each new vertex to a gate
evaluation, `DAGGate.eval_of_isNAND` (N1) and `DAGGate.eval_eq` give `!(a && b)`, `!!a = a`,
`!(!a && !b) = a || b`, `!true = false`, `!false = true` (`Bool` equation lemmas).  Depths:
`vertexDepth_last`, `vertexDepth_append` and `DAGGate.depth_eq`: one level for a copied `¬` gate
or `NAND[]`, two for the others.  New gates are `.not` gates of fan-in at most two by
`DAGGate.isNAND_iff`.  The fill needs a reader for `GadgetCorrect`, which has none at the issue
base (the owner-side `gadgetCorrect_iff`, plan section r3 §H2). -/
theorem nandGadget_correct :
    GadgetCorrect n 2 (fun _ l => l ≤ 2) DAGGate.IsNAND (nandGadget n) := by
  sorry

/-! ## The conversion -/

/-- **The NAND form of a circuit** whose gates read at most two vertices: the gate-rewriting host
applied to the NAND gadget, `C.toNANDForm hC = C.rewrite (nandGadget n) nandGadget_correct hC`.
The domain is `∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.args.length ≤ 2` (not `IsFaninTwo`: a `¬` gate of fan-in two is
already a NAND gate and is copied).  While N2 is admitted, `sorryAx` reaches this definition
through `nandGadget_correct` only.  Glue; motivated by [BV14, Def 2.13, p008-b002;
Thm 3.5, p014-b001]. -/
def DAGCircuit.toNANDForm (C : DAGCircuit n) (hC : ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.args.length ≤ 2) :
    DAGCircuit n :=
  C.rewrite (nandGadget n) nandGadget_correct hC

/-- The NAND form unfolded:
`C.toNANDForm hC = C.rewrite (nandGadget n) nandGadget_correct hC`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.toNANDForm_eq (C : DAGCircuit n) (hC : ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.args.length ≤ 2) :
    C.toNANDForm hC = C.rewrite (nandGadget n) nandGadget_correct hC := rfl

section ToNANDForm

variable (C : DAGCircuit n) (hC : ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.args.length ≤ 2)

/-- **N3. Semantics.** The NAND form computes the same function:
`(C.toNANDForm hC).eval x = C.eval x`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `toNANDForm_eq`, then `DAGCircuit.rewrite_eval` (`DAGTransform.lean`) with the
gadget's correctness N2. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.toNANDForm_eval (x : Fin n → Bool) : (C.toNANDForm hC).eval x = C.eval x := by
  sorry

/-- **N4. Form.** The conversion is in NAND form: `(C.toNANDForm hC).IsNANDForm`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `isNANDForm_iff` and `toNANDForm_eq`, then `DAGCircuit.rewrite_new_gates`
(`DAGTransform.lean`): every gate of a rewritten circuit satisfies the gadget's output
predicate, here `DAGGate.IsNAND`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.toNANDForm_isNANDForm : (C.toNANDForm hC).IsNANDForm := by
  sorry

/-- **N5. Depth.** The conversion at most doubles the depth:
`(C.toNANDForm hC).depth ≤ 2 * C.depth`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `toNANDForm_eq`, then `DAGCircuit.rewrite_depth_le` (`DAGTransform.lean`)
with the depth factor `c = 2` of N2. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.toNANDForm_depth_le : (C.toNANDForm hC).depth ≤ 2 * C.depth := by
  sorry

/-- **N6. Size.** The conversion has at most `n + 4 · #gates` vertices:
`(C.toNANDForm hC).size ≤ n + 4 * C.gates.length`.  This is the generic `rewrite` bound
(`fan-in + 2 ≤ 4` gates per old gate), not the tight `3 · #gates` (disclosed).  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `DAGCircuit.size_eq` on both sides and `toNANDForm_eq`; then
`DAGCircuit.rewrite_length_le` (`DAGTransform.lean`) bounds the new gate count by
`∑_{g ∈ C.gates} (g.args.length + 2)`, and each summand is at most `4` by `hC`
(`List.sum_le_card_nsmul` or an induction on the gate list). -/
theorem DAGCircuit.toNANDForm_size_le : (C.toNANDForm hC).size ≤ n + 4 * C.gates.length := by
  sorry

end ToNANDForm

end BoolCircuit

Authors: TCSlib contributors

import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Tuple.Basic
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.NANDForm

/-!
# Layering NAND-form `DAGCircuit`s

A circuit is *layered* (`BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsLayered`) when every gate sits exactly one level
above each vertex it reads: `C.depthAt a + 1 = C.depthAt (n + i)` for every argument `a` of gate
`i`.  Inputs are at level `0` and fan-in-0 gates at level `1`, so a layered circuit evaluates
level by level.

The conversion `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerNAND` takes a NAND-form circuit `C` on `n ≥ 1` inputs
to a layered NAND-form circuit on the `2n` **literals** `x, ¬x` (`BoolCircuit.litInput`), of the
same depth and function.

**Why literals (the odd-gap finding).** Call a vertex's depth its level.  In a layered NAND
circuit whose only level-0 vertices are the positive inputs, induction on the level shows that
every vertex at an even level computes a monotone function and every vertex at an odd level an
antimonotone one (constants are both; the NAND of antimonotone functions is monotone, and
conversely).  XOR is neither, so over positive inputs no layering exists in general: an odd gap
cannot always be padded.  With both literals at level `0` every vertex is available at both
parities.  Literal inputs are Bar89's "inputs and negated inputs" [Bar89, Thm 1, p003-b002].

**Construction** (computable, by columns in topological order; no NAND-form hypothesis).  Write
`D := C.depth` and `δ := C.depthAt v`.  Each old vertex `v` with `δ ≤ D` gets a *column* of new
vertices `v@k`, one for every level `δ ≤ k ≤ D`, with `v@k` at depth exactly `k`:
* **base** `v@δ`: an input `xᵢ` is input vertex `i`; a gate is a NAND gate over its arguments'
  copies `a@(δ - 1)`;
* **parity twin** `v@(δ + 1)`: an input's twin is `NAND(¬xᵢ)`, reading input vertex `n + i`; a
  gate's twin is the same NAND gate over `a@δ`; a fan-in-0 gate's twin is `NAND(NAND(x₀, ¬x₀))`,
  which needs `n ≥ 1`;
* **double-NAND chain** `v@k = NAND(NAND(v@(k - 2)))` for `k ≥ δ + 2`, the inner gate at level
  `k - 1`.

Every gate is emitted as a NAND gate `⟨.not, args⟩`.  Old vertices deeper than `D` are dead and
get no column.  The output is `out@D`.  The gate list (`layerGates`) and output vertex
(`layerOutput`) are definitions; the structure fields of `DAGCircuit` (acyclicity, output in
range) are the targets N12–N13, as N2 is for `toNANDForm`, so while they are admitted `sorryAx`
reaches `layerNAND` through them only.

**Column invariant** (the plan of every target's fill): after the fold has processed the old
vertices `0, …, v - 1`, for every processed `u` with `C.depthAt u ≤ D` and every level
`C.depthAt u ≤ k ≤ D`, the recorded vertex `u@k` exists below the current vertex count, has depth
exactly `k`, reads only vertices of depth `k - 1`, and, when `C.IsNANDForm`, has on
`litInput x` the value of `u` on `x`; the column of `u` has at most `2 (D - C.depthAt u) + 1`
gates.  It is proved by induction along the fold.

**Not reused.** `DAGCircuit.toLayered` and `TreeCircuit.toLayered` (`LayeredDAG.lean`) map into
the other model `LayeredCircuit` with one vertex per layer (depth = number of gates) and need
`IsWellFormed` and no `∨`; the conversion here keeps the `DAGCircuit` model and its depth, and is
named `layerNAND`, not `toLayered`.  It is not an instance of `DAGCircuit.rewrite`: the input
count changes and the depth must be exact, not bounded.  The column fold is a construction, not
a host: its contract does not vary by consumer.

No ingested passage defines layered circuits or a layering conversion: the conversion is glue,
motivated by the level-by-level evaluation of [BV11, Thm 3.1, p015-b001; Def 3.6, p014-b001]
("depth-`L` binary arithmetic circuits", an evaluation key whose length depends on `L`).

## Main definitions

* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsLayered` — every gate is one level above each vertex it reads.
* `BoolCircuit.litInput` — the `2n` literals of an input.
* `BoolCircuit.layerChain`, `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerAt`, `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerColumn`,
  `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerFold` — the column builder.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerGates`, `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerOutput` — the gates and the
  output vertex of the layering.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerNAND` — the layering conversion.

## Main results

All are statement-phase targets (glue):
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerGates_acyclic`, `layerOutput_lt` (N12–N13) — the structure fields.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerNAND_eval` (N7) — semantics on the literal input.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerNAND_isLayered` (N8), `layerNAND_isNANDForm` (N9).
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerNAND_depth` (N10) — depth preserved exactly.
* `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.layerNAND_size_le` (N11) — size `≤ 2n + (2 · depth + 1) · size`.

## References

* [Bar89] D. A. Barrington, *Bounded-width polynomial-size branching programs recognize exactly
  those languages in NC¹*, J. Comput. Syst. Sci. 38(1):150–164, 1989.
* [BV11] Z. Brakerski, V. Vaikuntanathan, *Efficient fully homomorphic encryption from (standard)
  LWE*, FOCS 2011 (full version).
-/

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace BoolCircuit

variable {n : ℕ}

/-! ## Layered circuits and literal inputs -/

/-- `C` is *layered*: every gate sits exactly one level above each vertex it reads,
`C.depthAt a + 1 = C.depthAt (n + i)` for every argument `a` of every gate `i` (inputs at level
`0`).  Glue, motivated by the level-by-level evaluation of [BV11, Thm 3.1, p015-b001;
Def 3.6, p014-b001]. -/
def DAGCircuit.IsLayered (C : DAGCircuit n) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < C.gates.length), ∀ a ∈ (C.gates[i]).args,
    C.depthAt a + 1 = C.depthAt (n + i)

/-- Layeredness unfolded: `C.IsLayered ↔ ∀ i (hi : i < C.gates.length), ∀ a ∈ (C.gates[i]).args,
C.depthAt a + 1 = C.depthAt (n + i)`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.isLayered_iff (C : DAGCircuit n) :
    C.IsLayered ↔ ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < C.gates.length), ∀ a ∈ (C.gates[i]).args,
      C.depthAt a + 1 = C.depthAt (n + i) :=
  Iff.rfl

instance DAGCircuit.decidableIsLayered (C : DAGCircuit n) : Decidable C.IsLayered :=
  @Nat.decidableBallLT C.gates.length
    (fun i hi => ∀ a ∈ (C.gates[i]).args, C.depthAt a + 1 = C.depthAt (n + i))
    (fun i hi => List.decidableBAll _ _)

/-- The *literal input* of `x`: the `2n` literals, positive ones first,
`litInput x = Fin.append x (fun i => !x i)` (Bar89's "inputs and negated inputs"
[Bar89, Thm 1, p003-b002]). -/
def litInput (x : Fin n → Bool) : Fin (n + n) → Bool := Fin.append x fun i => !x i

/-- The literal input unfolded: `litInput x = Fin.append x (fun i => !x i)`. -/
theorem litInput_eq (x : Fin n → Bool) : litInput x = Fin.append x fun i => !x i := rfl

/-- The positive half of the literal input: `litInput x (Fin.castAdd n i) = x i`. -/
theorem litInput_castAdd (x : Fin n → Bool) (i : Fin n) : litInput x (Fin.castAdd n i) = x i := by
  rw [litInput_eq, Fin.append_left]

/-- The negative half of the literal input: `litInput x (Fin.natAdd n i) = !x i`. -/
theorem litInput_natAdd (x : Fin n → Bool) (i : Fin n) : litInput x (Fin.natAdd n i) = !x i := by
  rw [litInput_eq, Fin.append_right]

/-! ## The column builder -/

/-- The **double-NAND chain**: after the gates `gs` of a circuit with `N` inputs, with `a` and
`b` the copies of a vertex at the two levels below the next one, append `s` links; link `t`
appends the inner gate `NAND(a)` (vertex `N + |gs|`) and the outer gate `NAND(NAND(a))` (vertex
`N + |gs| + 1`), which becomes the copy two levels above `a`.  Returns the new gate list and the
outer vertices, in level order:
`layerChain N gs a b 0 = (gs, [])` and `layerChain N gs a b (s + 1) =
let r := layerChain N (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [N + |gs|]⟩]) b (N + |gs| + 1) s;
(r.1, (N + |gs| + 1) :: r.2)`.  Glue (plan section r3 §H3.13). -/
def layerChain (N : ℕ) : List DAGGate → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → List DAGGate × List ℕ
  | gs, _, _, 0 => (gs, [])
  | gs, a, b, s + 1 =>
    let r := layerChain N (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [N + gs.length]⟩]) b (N + gs.length + 1) s
    (r.1, (N + gs.length + 1) :: r.2)

/-- The empty chain: `layerChain N gs a b 0 = (gs, [])`. -/
theorem layerChain_zero (N : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) (a b : ℕ) :
    layerChain N gs a b 0 = (gs, []) := rfl

/-- One more link: `layerChain N gs a b (s + 1) = ((layerChain N gs' b (N + |gs| + 1) s).1,
(N + |gs| + 1) :: (layerChain N gs' b (N + |gs| + 1) s).2)` with
`gs' = gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [N + |gs|]⟩]`. -/
theorem layerChain_succ (N : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) (a b s : ℕ) :
    layerChain N gs a b (s + 1) =
      ((layerChain N (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [N + gs.length]⟩]) b (N + gs.length + 1) s).1,
        (N + gs.length + 1) ::
          (layerChain N (gs ++ [⟨.not, [a]⟩, ⟨.not, [N + gs.length]⟩]) b
            (N + gs.length + 1) s).2) := rfl

/-- The copy `v@k` recorded in the columns `cols` (column `v` lists `v@δ, v@(δ + 1), …` with
`δ = C.depthAt v`): `C.layerAt cols v k = (cols.getD v []).getD (k - C.depthAt v) 0`.  Glue. -/
def DAGCircuit.layerAt (C : DAGCircuit n) (cols : List (List ℕ)) (v k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (cols.getD v []).getD (k - C.depthAt v) 0

/-- The recorded copy unfolded: `C.layerAt cols v k = (cols.getD v []).getD (k - C.depthAt v) 0`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerAt_eq (C : DAGCircuit n) (cols : List (List ℕ)) (v k : ℕ) :
    C.layerAt cols v k = (cols.getD v []).getD (k - C.depthAt v) 0 := rfl

/-- One step of the column fold: build the column of the old vertex `v` after the state
`s = (new gates, columns of 0, …, v - 1)`, over the `n + n` literal inputs.  With `D = C.depth`,
`δ = C.depthAt v` and `m = n + n + |s.1|` (the next new vertex):
* `D < δ` (dead vertex): no gate, empty column;
* `v < n` (input), `D = 0`: column `[v]`;
* `v < n`, `D ≥ 1`: twin `NAND[n + v]` (vertex `m`), then `D - 1` chain links from `(v, m)`;
  column `v :: m :: chain`;
* gate `g = C.gates.getD (v - n) ⟨.not, []⟩`: base `NAND[a@(δ - 1) | a ∈ g.args]` (vertex `m`);
  if `D = δ` the column is `[m]`; otherwise the twin is `NAND[a@δ | a ∈ g.args]` (vertex
  `m + 1`), or, when `g.args = []`, `NAND[0, n]` then `NAND[m + 1]` (twin vertex `m + 2`); then
  `D - δ - 1` chain links from `(m, twin)`; column `m :: twin :: chain`.
Glue (plan section r3 §H3.13). -/
def DAGCircuit.layerColumn (C : DAGCircuit n) (s : List DAGGate × List (List ℕ)) (v : ℕ) :
    List DAGGate × List (List ℕ) :=
  if C.depth < C.depthAt v then (s.1, s.2 ++ [[]])
  else if v < n then
    if C.depth = 0 then (s.1, s.2 ++ [[v]])
    else
      let r := layerChain (n + n) (s.1 ++ [⟨.not, [n + v]⟩]) v (n + n + s.1.length) (C.depth - 1)
      (r.1, s.2 ++ [v :: (n + n + s.1.length) :: r.2])
  else
    let g := C.gates.getD (v - n) ⟨.not, []⟩
    let m := n + n + s.1.length
    let gs₁ := s.1 ++ [⟨.not, g.args.map fun a => C.layerAt s.2 a (C.depthAt v - 1)⟩]
    if C.depth = C.depthAt v then (gs₁, s.2 ++ [[m]])
    else
      let tw : List DAGGate × ℕ :=
        if g.args = [] then (gs₁ ++ [⟨.not, [0, n]⟩, ⟨.not, [m + 1]⟩], m + 2)
        else (gs₁ ++ [⟨.not, g.args.map fun a => C.layerAt s.2 a (C.depthAt v)⟩], m + 1)
      let r := layerChain (n + n) tw.1 m tw.2 (C.depth - C.depthAt v - 1)
      (r.1, s.2 ++ [m :: tw.2 :: r.2])

/-- The fold step unfolded (`C.layerColumn s v` is the case split of its docstring).

**Proof sketch.** Definitional: `rfl`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerColumn_eq (C : DAGCircuit n) (s : List DAGGate × List (List ℕ)) (v : ℕ) :
    C.layerColumn s v =
      if C.depth < C.depthAt v then (s.1, s.2 ++ [[]])
      else if v < n then
        if C.depth = 0 then (s.1, s.2 ++ [[v]])
        else
          ((layerChain (n + n) (s.1 ++ [⟨.not, [n + v]⟩]) v (n + n + s.1.length)
              (C.depth - 1)).1,
            s.2 ++ [v :: (n + n + s.1.length) ::
              (layerChain (n + n) (s.1 ++ [⟨.not, [n + v]⟩]) v (n + n + s.1.length)
                (C.depth - 1)).2])
      else
        if C.depth = C.depthAt v then
          (s.1 ++ [⟨.not, (C.gates.getD (v - n) ⟨.not, []⟩).args.map fun a =>
              C.layerAt s.2 a (C.depthAt v - 1)⟩], s.2 ++ [[n + n + s.1.length]])
        else
          let gs₁ := s.1 ++ [⟨.not, (C.gates.getD (v - n) ⟨.not, []⟩).args.map fun a =>
              C.layerAt s.2 a (C.depthAt v - 1)⟩]
          let tw : List DAGGate × ℕ :=
            if (C.gates.getD (v - n) ⟨.not, []⟩).args = [] then
              (gs₁ ++ [⟨.not, [0, n]⟩, ⟨.not, [n + n + s.1.length + 1]⟩],
                n + n + s.1.length + 2)
            else
              (gs₁ ++ [⟨.not, (C.gates.getD (v - n) ⟨.not, []⟩).args.map fun a =>
                C.layerAt s.2 a (C.depthAt v)⟩], n + n + s.1.length + 1)
          ((layerChain (n + n) tw.1 (n + n + s.1.length) tw.2
              (C.depth - C.depthAt v - 1)).1,
            s.2 ++ [(n + n + s.1.length) :: tw.2 ::
              (layerChain (n + n) tw.1 (n + n + s.1.length) tw.2
                (C.depth - C.depthAt v - 1)).2]) := rfl

/-- The column fold over the old vertices `0, …, n + |C.gates| - 1` in topological order:
`C.layerFold = (List.range (n + C.gates.length)).foldl C.layerColumn ([], [])`.  Glue. -/
def DAGCircuit.layerFold (C : DAGCircuit n) : List DAGGate × List (List ℕ) :=
  (List.range (n + C.gates.length)).foldl C.layerColumn ([], [])

/-- The column fold unfolded:
`C.layerFold = (List.range (n + C.gates.length)).foldl C.layerColumn ([], [])`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerFold_eq (C : DAGCircuit n) :
    C.layerFold = (List.range (n + C.gates.length)).foldl C.layerColumn ([], []) := rfl

/-- The gate list of the layering (plan section r3 §H3.13): `C.layerGates = C.layerFold.1`, every
old vertex `v` realized at each level `C.depthAt v ≤ k ≤ C.depth` (base, parity twin, double-NAND
chain), every gate emitted as a NAND gate, columns in topological order.  Computable; glue
(no ingested source, r3 §H1 gap 4). -/
def DAGCircuit.layerGates [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n) : List DAGGate := C.layerFold.1

/-- The layering's gates unfolded: `C.layerGates = C.layerFold.1`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerGates_eq [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n) :
    C.layerGates = C.layerFold.1 := rfl

/-- The output vertex of the layering, `out@(C.depth)`:
`C.layerOutput = C.layerAt C.layerFold.2 C.output C.depth`.  Computable; glue. -/
def DAGCircuit.layerOutput [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n) : ℕ :=
  C.layerAt C.layerFold.2 C.output C.depth

/-- The layering's output unfolded: `C.layerOutput = C.layerAt C.layerFold.2 C.output C.depth`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerOutput_eq [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n) :
    C.layerOutput = C.layerAt C.layerFold.2 C.output C.depth := rfl

/-! ## The structure fields (targets) -/

/-- **N12. Acyclicity of the layering.** Every gate of `C.layerGates` reads only earlier vertices
of the circuit on `n + n` inputs: `∀ (i : ℕ) (h : i < C.layerGates.length),
∀ a ∈ (C.layerGates[i]).args, a < n + n + i` (the `args_lt` field of `DAGCircuit (n + n)`, i.e.
`GatesAcyclic (n + n) C.layerGates`).  Glue.

Stated in the field's form rather than as `GatesAcyclic (n + n) C.layerGates` (plan section r3
§H5.6b): `GatesAcyclic` (`DAGCircuit.lean`) has no published reader, and filling the field from a
`GatesAcyclic` proof would unfold it (Rule 10).  The meaning is identical (the body of
`GatesAcyclic`).

**Proof sketch.** Induction along the fold (`layerFold_eq`, `List.foldl` over `List.range`) with
the column invariant of the module docstring, part "every recorded copy lies below the current
vertex count": each step (`layerColumn_eq`) appends gates that read `n + v` or `0, n` (inputs,
below `n + n` by `NeZero n`), the recorded copies of earlier vertices (below the count by the
invariant; the arguments `a` of gate `v - n` satisfy `a < v` by `C.args_lt`), or the gates just
appended (`layerChain_succ`: the inner gate `N + |gs|` precedes the outer one).  Each appended
gate's arguments are therefore below its own vertex `n + n + i`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerGates_acyclic [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n) :
    ∀ (i : ℕ) (h : i < C.layerGates.length), ∀ a ∈ (C.layerGates[i]).args, a < n + n + i := by
  sorry

/-- **N13. The output is a vertex.** `C.layerOutput < (n + n) + C.layerGates.length` (the
`output_lt` field of `DAGCircuit (n + n)`).  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** The output's column exists because `C.depthAt C.output = C.depth`
(`DAGCircuit.depth_eq`) and `C.output < n + C.gates.length` (`C.output_lt`), so the fold visits
it and does not take the dead branch; its first entry is `out@D` (`layerOutput_eq`,
`layerAt_eq`, index `D - D = 0`), which by the column invariant is below the vertex count
`n + n + |C.layerGates|`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerOutput_lt [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n) :
    C.layerOutput < (n + n) + C.layerGates.length := by
  sorry

/-! ## The conversion -/

/-- **The layering conversion** (plan section r3 §H3.13): the circuit on the `n + n` literal
inputs with gates `C.layerGates` and output `C.layerOutput`,
`C.layerNAND = ⟨C.layerGates, C.layerOutput, N12, N13⟩` (field readers `layerNAND_gates`,
`layerNAND_output`, generated by `simps`, not `@[simp]`).  While N12 and N13 are admitted,
`sorryAx` reaches it through them only.  Glue (no ingested source, r3 §H1 gap 4); motivated by
[BV11, Thm 3.1, p015-b001; Def 3.6, p014-b001]. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) gates output]
def DAGCircuit.layerNAND [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n) : DAGCircuit (n + n) where
  gates := C.layerGates
  output := C.layerOutput
  args_lt := C.layerGates_acyclic
  output_lt := C.layerOutput_lt

section LayerNAND

variable [NeZero n] (C : DAGCircuit n)

/-- **N7. Semantics on the literal input.** For a NAND-form circuit the layering computes the same
function on the literals: `C.IsNANDForm → C.layerNAND.eval (litInput x) = C.eval x`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** The column invariant, value part, at the output: by induction along the fold,
every recorded copy `v@k` has on `litInput x` the value of `v` on `x`.  Inputs: `v@0` is input
vertex `v` (`DAGCircuit.values_getD_input`, `litInput_castAdd`); the twin `NAND(¬xᵥ)` reads
vertex `n + v` (`litInput_natAdd`) and gives `!!xᵥ = xᵥ` (`DAGGate.eval_of_isNAND`, N1).
Gates: the old gate is a NAND gate (`DAGCircuit.isNANDForm_iff`, `DAGGate.eval_of_isNAND`) and
the base and twin read copies with the same values (`DAGCircuit.values_getD_gate`); a fan-in-0
twin gives `!(!(x₀ && !x₀)) = false`.  A chain link gives `!!b = b`.  Read off at
`out@D` with `DAGCircuit.eval_eq` and `layerNAND_output`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerNAND_eval (hC : C.IsNANDForm) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    C.layerNAND.eval (litInput x) = C.eval x := by
  sorry

/-- **N8. Layered.** `C.layerNAND.IsLayered`, with no hypothesis: every new gate reads only copies
one level down.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `isLayered_iff`, then the column invariant, depth part: every recorded copy
`v@k` has depth exactly `k` (`DAGCircuit.depthAt_gate`, `DAGGate.depth_eq`; the depth of a gate
does not depend on its kind, so no NAND-form hypothesis is needed), and every gate appended at
level `k` reads only vertices of depth `k - 1`: the base reads `a@(δ - 1)`, the twin `a@δ` (or
inputs `0, n` through the inner gate), a chain link `v@(k - 2)` through the inner gate at level
`k - 1`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerNAND_isLayered : C.layerNAND.IsLayered := by
  sorry

/-- **N9. NAND form.** `C.IsNANDForm → C.layerNAND.IsNANDForm`: every gate is emitted as a `¬`
gate, and the copies keep the old fan-in, so `hC` is needed for fan-in `≤ 2`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `isNANDForm_iff`, `DAGGate.isNAND_iff` and `layerNAND_gates`: induction along the
fold (`layerFold_eq`, `layerColumn_eq`, `layerChain_succ`); every appended gate is
`⟨.not, args⟩` with `args` of length `1` (chain, input twin), `2` (`NAND[0, n]`) or the old
gate's fan-in (base and twin, `List.length_map`), which is at most `2` by `hC`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerNAND_isNANDForm (hC : C.IsNANDForm) : C.layerNAND.IsNANDForm := by
  sorry

/-- **N10. Depth is preserved exactly.** `C.layerNAND.depth = C.depth`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `DAGCircuit.depth_eq` and `layerNAND_output`: the output is `out@D` with
`D = C.depth` (`layerOutput_eq`), and by the column invariant, depth part, it has depth exactly
`D`. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerNAND_depth : C.layerNAND.depth = C.depth := by
  sorry

/-- **N11. Size.** `C.layerNAND.size ≤ 2 * n + (2 * C.depth + 1) * C.size`.  Glue.

Constant settled at the statement phase: with `D = C.depth` and `δ = C.depthAt v`, the column of
an input has `0` gates (`D = 0`) or `1 + 2 (D - 1) = 2D - 1` (twin and chain); the column of a live
gate has `1` (base) when `δ = D`, otherwise `1 + 1 + 2 (D - δ - 1) = 2 (D - δ)` gates, or
`2 (D - δ) + 1` for a fan-in-0 gate (two-gate twin); a dead vertex has none.  Every column has at
most `2D + 1` gates, so `|C.layerGates| ≤ (2D + 1) (n + |C.gates|)`, and the size is
`(n + n) + |C.layerGates| ≤ 2n + (2D + 1) · C.size`.

**Proof sketch.** `DAGCircuit.size_eq` (both circuits) and `layerNAND_gates`; induction along the
fold with the column-length part of the invariant (each step appends at most `2D + 1` gates:
`layerColumn_eq`, `layerChain` appends exactly two gates per link), summed over the
`n + |C.gates|` old vertices. -/
theorem DAGCircuit.layerNAND_size_le : C.layerNAND.size ≤ 2 * n + (2 * C.depth + 1) * C.size := by
  sorry

end LayerNAND

end BoolCircuit

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.TreeDAG

/-!
# Formula combinators: the balanced binary gate

The first rows of the circuit and formula gadget registry (`machine-library-design.md`, "Circuit
and formula gadgets"): combinators on `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit` formulas that the formula
arithmetic of `FormulaArith/` is built from.  This file starts with the balanced binary tree of
gates, `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.balanced`, which computes an unbounded `∧`/`∨` gate with fan-in
two at logarithmic extra depth.  It was the private `combine` of `TreeNCAC.lean`, promoted
unchanged; `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.toBinary` now calls it from there.

## Main definitions

* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.balanced` — the balanced binary tree of `b`-gates over a child list.
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.neg` — the De Morgan negation (literals flip sign, gates flip
  kind), depth- and fan-in-preserving.
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.subst` — substitution of formulas for variables (a negative
  literal becomes the negated formula).  Its literal case, renaming the variables, is the
  existing `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx` (`BooleanAnalysis/LMN/CircuitReindex.lean`).
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.const` — the constant formula `node b []`.
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.and2`, `or2`, `xor2`, `xor3`, `maj3` — the fan-in-2 gadgets, of
  depth `+1`, `+1`, `+2`, `+4`, `+3` over their arguments.

## Main results

* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.balanced_eval` — it computes the unbounded gate.
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.maxFanin_balanced_le`, `depth_balanced_le`, `size_balanced_le` —
  fan-in two, `⌈log₂ |cs|⌉ + 1` extra depth, `|cs| + 1` extra size.
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.balanced_nil`, `balanced_singleton` — the readers on short lists.
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.neg_eval`, `depth_neg`, `maxFanin_neg` — negation (F1; targets).
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.subst_eval`, `depth_subst_le`, `maxFanin_subst_le` — substitution
  (F2; targets).
* `BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.const_eval`, `xor3_eval`, `maj3_eval`, and the value, depth and
  fan-in lemmas of every gadget (F3; targets).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace BoolCircuit

variable {n : ℕ}

/-! ### Simulating an unbounded gate by a balanced binary tree -/

/-- Pair adjacent children under a gate of type `b`, halving the list. -/
private def pairUp (b : Bool) : List (TreeCircuit n) → List (TreeCircuit n)
  | [] => []
  | [c] => [c]
  | c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => TreeCircuit.node b [c₁, c₂] :: pairUp b cs

/-- Pairing halves the list, rounding up. -/
private theorem length_pairUp (b : Bool) :
    ∀ cs : List (TreeCircuit n), (pairUp b cs).length = (cs.length + 1) / 2
  | [] => by simp [pairUp]
  | [_] => by simp [pairUp]
  | _ :: _ :: cs => by
      have := length_pairUp b cs
      simp only [pairUp, List.length_cons] at *
      omega

/-- Pairing preserves the value of the surrounding gate. -/
private theorem eval_node_pairUp (b : Bool) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    ∀ cs : List (TreeCircuit n),
      (TreeCircuit.node b (pairUp b cs)).eval x = (TreeCircuit.node b cs).eval x
  | [] => rfl
  | [_] => by cases b <;> simp [pairUp, TreeCircuit.eval_node_true, TreeCircuit.eval_node_false]
  | c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => by
      have := eval_node_pairUp b x cs
      cases b <;>
        simp only [pairUp, TreeCircuit.eval_node_true, TreeCircuit.eval_node_false,
          List.all_cons, List.all_nil, List.any_cons, List.any_nil] at * <;>
        simp [this, Bool.and_assoc, Bool.or_assoc]

/-- Pairing adds at most one to the depth. -/
private theorem maxDepth_pairUp (b : Bool) :
    ∀ cs : List (TreeCircuit n), TreeCircuit.maxDepth (pairUp b cs) ≤ 1 + TreeCircuit.maxDepth cs
  | [] => by simp [pairUp, TreeCircuit.maxDepth_nil]
  | [c] => by simp [pairUp]
  | c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => by
      have ih := maxDepth_pairUp b cs
      have h1 : (TreeCircuit.node b [c₁, c₂]).depth
          = 1 + max c₁.depth (max c₂.depth 0) := by
        rw [TreeCircuit.depth_node, TreeCircuit.maxDepth_cons, TreeCircuit.maxDepth_cons,
          TreeCircuit.maxDepth_nil]
      simp only [pairUp, TreeCircuit.maxDepth_cons, h1]
      omega

/-- Pairing does not increase the total size plus length. -/
private theorem sumSize_pairUp (b : Bool) :
    ∀ cs : List (TreeCircuit n),
      TreeCircuit.sumSize (pairUp b cs) + (pairUp b cs).length ≤
        TreeCircuit.sumSize cs + cs.length
  | [] => by rw [pairUp, TreeCircuit.sumSize_nil, List.length_nil]
  | [_] => le_refl _
  | c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => by
      have ih := sumSize_pairUp b cs
      have h1 : (TreeCircuit.node b [c₁, c₂]).size = 1 + (c₁.size + (c₂.size + 0)) := by
        rw [TreeCircuit.size_node, TreeCircuit.sumSize_cons, TreeCircuit.sumSize_cons,
          TreeCircuit.sumSize_nil]
      simp only [pairUp, TreeCircuit.sumSize_cons, h1, List.length_cons]
      omega

/-- Pairing introduces only fan-in-2 gates. -/
private theorem maxFaninL_pairUp (b : Bool) :
    ∀ cs : List (TreeCircuit n),
      TreeCircuit.maxFaninL (pairUp b cs) ≤ max 2 (TreeCircuit.maxFaninL cs)
  | [] => by rw [pairUp, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_nil]; exact Nat.zero_le _
  | [c] => by simp [pairUp, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_cons, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_nil]
  | c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => by
      have ih := maxFaninL_pairUp b cs
      have h1 : (TreeCircuit.node b [c₁, c₂]).maxFanin
          = max 2 (max c₁.maxFanin (max c₂.maxFanin 0)) := by
        rw [TreeCircuit.maxFanin_node, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_cons, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_cons,
          TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_nil]
        norm_num
      simp only [pairUp, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_cons, h1]
      omega

/-- Repeatedly pair a child list, `k` rounds at most, into a single circuit. -/
private def combineFuel (b : Bool) : ℕ → List (TreeCircuit n) → TreeCircuit n
  | 0, cs => TreeCircuit.node b cs
  | _ + 1, [] => TreeCircuit.node b []
  | _ + 1, [c] => c
  | k + 1, c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => combineFuel b k (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs))

/-- The balanced binary tree of `b`-gates over the child list `cs`: the children are paired
under fan-in-2 `b`-gates round by round (at most `|cs|` rounds) until one circuit is left,
`balanced b cs = combineFuel b |cs| cs`.  It computes the unbounded gate
`TreeCircuit.node b cs` (`TreeCircuit.balanced_eval`); `balanced b [] = node b []` and
`balanced b [c] = c`.  The former private `TreeNCAC.combine`, promoted for the formula
arithmetic layer; glue behind [AB09, p. 118]'s fan-in reduction (`TreeCircuit.toBinary`). -/
def TreeCircuit.balanced (b : Bool) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)) : TreeCircuit n :=
  combineFuel b cs.length cs

/-- Combining computes the same value as the unbounded gate. -/
private theorem combineFuel_eval (b : Bool) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)),
      (combineFuel b k cs).eval x = (TreeCircuit.node b cs).eval x
  | 0, _ => rfl
  | _ + 1, [] => rfl
  | _ + 1, [c] => by
      cases b <;> simp [combineFuel, TreeCircuit.eval_node_true, TreeCircuit.eval_node_false]
  | k + 1, c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => by
      show (combineFuel b k (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs))).eval x = _
      rw [combineFuel_eval b x k, eval_node_pairUp]

/-- Combining produces only fan-in-2 gates, given enough rounds. -/
private theorem combineFuel_maxFanin (b : Bool) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)), cs.length ≤ k →
      (combineFuel b k cs).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (TreeCircuit.maxFaninL cs)
  | 0, [], _ => by simp [combineFuel, TreeCircuit.maxFanin_node, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_nil]
  | 0, _ :: _, h => by simp at h
  | _ + 1, [], _ => by simp [combineFuel, TreeCircuit.maxFanin_node, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_nil]
  | _ + 1, [c], _ => by
      show c.maxFanin ≤ _
      rw [TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_cons, TreeCircuit.maxFaninL_nil]
      omega
  | k + 1, c₁ :: c₂ :: cs, h => by
      have hp := length_pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)
      have hlen : (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)).length ≤ k := by
        simp only [List.length_cons] at h hp ⊢; omega
      have ih := combineFuel_maxFanin b k _ hlen
      have h2 := maxFaninL_pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)
      show (combineFuel b k (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs))).maxFanin ≤ _
      omega

/-- Combining `m` children costs `⌈log₂ m⌉` extra levels of depth.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the fuel.  With no children, or one child, the bound is
immediate.  With at least two children, one round of pairing halves the list (to
`⌈m / 2⌉` entries) and raises the maximum child depth by at most one, while
`⌈log₂ m⌉ = ⌈log₂ ⌈m / 2⌉⌉ + 1` for `m ≥ 2`; the induction hypothesis on the paired list
then gives the bound. -/
private theorem combineFuel_depth (b : Bool) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)), cs.length ≤ k →
      (combineFuel b k cs).depth ≤ TreeCircuit.maxDepth cs + Nat.clog 2 cs.length + 1
  | 0, [], _ => by simp [combineFuel, TreeCircuit.depth_node, TreeCircuit.maxDepth_nil]
  | 0, _ :: _, h => by simp at h
  | _ + 1, [], _ => by simp [combineFuel, TreeCircuit.depth_node, TreeCircuit.maxDepth_nil]
  | _ + 1, [c], _ => by
      show c.depth ≤ _
      rw [TreeCircuit.maxDepth_cons, TreeCircuit.maxDepth_nil]
      simp
  | k + 1, c₁ :: c₂ :: cs, h => by
      have hp := length_pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)
      have hlen : (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)).length ≤ k := by
        simp only [List.length_cons] at h hp ⊢; omega
      have ih := combineFuel_depth b k _ hlen
      have h2 := maxDepth_pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)
      have hclog : Nat.clog 2 (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs).length
          = Nat.clog 2 ((pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)).length) + 1 := by
        rw [hp]
        have := Nat.clog_of_two_le (b := 2) (n := (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs).length)
          (by norm_num) (by simp)
        simpa using this
      show (combineFuel b k (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs))).depth ≤ _
      omega

/-- Combining `m` children costs at most `m` extra gates. -/
private theorem combineFuel_size (b : Bool) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)),
      (combineFuel b k cs).size ≤ TreeCircuit.sumSize cs + cs.length + 1
  | 0, cs => by show (TreeCircuit.node b cs).size ≤ _; rw [TreeCircuit.size_node]; omega
  | _ + 1, [] => by simp [combineFuel, TreeCircuit.size_node, TreeCircuit.sumSize_nil]
  | _ + 1, [c] => by show c.size ≤ _; rw [TreeCircuit.sumSize_cons, TreeCircuit.sumSize_nil]; omega
  | k + 1, c₁ :: c₂ :: cs => by
      have ih := combineFuel_size b k (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs))
      have h2 := sumSize_pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs)
      show (combineFuel b k (pairUp b (c₁ :: c₂ :: cs))).size ≤ _
      omega

/-- The balanced tree computes the unbounded gate:
`(TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).eval x = (TreeCircuit.node b cs).eval x`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.balanced_eval (b : Bool) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).eval x = (TreeCircuit.node b cs).eval x :=
  combineFuel_eval b x _ cs

/-- The balanced tree has fan-in 2, unless a child already had more:
`(TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (TreeCircuit.maxFaninL cs)`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_balanced_le (b : Bool) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)) :
    (TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (TreeCircuit.maxFaninL cs) :=
  combineFuel_maxFanin b _ cs (le_refl _)

/-- The balanced tree adds at most `⌈log₂ |cs|⌉ + 1` to the children's depth:
`(TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).depth ≤ TreeCircuit.maxDepth cs + Nat.clog 2 cs.length + 1`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_balanced_le (b : Bool) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)) :
    (TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).depth ≤ TreeCircuit.maxDepth cs + Nat.clog 2 cs.length + 1 :=
  combineFuel_depth b _ cs (le_refl _)

/-- The balanced tree adds at most `|cs| + 1` to the children's total size:
`(TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).size ≤ TreeCircuit.sumSize cs + cs.length + 1`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.size_balanced_le (b : Bool) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)) :
    (TreeCircuit.balanced b cs).size ≤ TreeCircuit.sumSize cs + cs.length + 1 :=
  combineFuel_size b _ cs

/-- The balanced tree over no children is the empty gate: `TreeCircuit.balanced b [] =
TreeCircuit.node b []`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.balanced_nil (b : Bool) :
    TreeCircuit.balanced b ([] : List (TreeCircuit n)) = TreeCircuit.node b [] := rfl

/-- The balanced tree over one child is that child: `TreeCircuit.balanced b [c] = c`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.balanced_singleton (b : Bool) (c : TreeCircuit n) :
    TreeCircuit.balanced b [c] = c := rfl

/-! ### De Morgan negation and substitution (F1–F2) -/

mutual

/-- The De Morgan negation of a formula: every literal flips its sign and every gate flips its
kind, `(lit ⟨i, s⟩).neg = lit ⟨i, !s⟩` and `(node b cs).neg = node (!b) (cs.map neg)`, so
that `c.neg` computes `!c.eval x` with the same shape, depth and fan-in
(`TreeCircuit.neg_eval`, `depth_neg`, `maxFanin_neg`).  Structural recursion over the nested
child list, through the private list helper `negList`.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.neg : TreeCircuit n → TreeCircuit n
  | .lit l => .lit ⟨l.idx, !l.sign⟩
  | .node b cs => .node (!b) (negList cs)

/-- `TreeCircuit.neg` on every member of a child list: `negList cs = cs.map neg`. -/
private def negList : List (TreeCircuit n) → List (TreeCircuit n)
  | [] => []
  | c :: cs => c.neg :: negList cs

end

/-- The negation of a literal flips its sign:
`(TreeCircuit.lit l).neg = TreeCircuit.lit ⟨l.idx, !l.sign⟩`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.neg_lit (l : Lit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.lit l).neg = TreeCircuit.lit ⟨l.idx, !l.sign⟩ := rfl

/-- The list helper of `neg` is `List.map`: `negList cs = cs.map TreeCircuit.neg`. -/
private theorem negList_eq_map : ∀ cs : List (TreeCircuit n), negList cs = cs.map TreeCircuit.neg
  | [] => rfl
  | c :: cs => congrArg (c.neg :: ·) (negList_eq_map cs)

/-- The negation of a gate flips its kind and negates every child:
`(TreeCircuit.node b cs).neg = TreeCircuit.node (!b) (cs.map TreeCircuit.neg)`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.neg_node (b : Bool) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n)) :
    (TreeCircuit.node b cs).neg = TreeCircuit.node (!b) (cs.map TreeCircuit.neg) :=
  congrArg (TreeCircuit.node (!b)) (negList_eq_map cs)

/-- **F1, value.** The De Morgan negation computes the negation:
`c.neg.eval x = !c.eval x`.  Glue (r3 §H5.7, F1).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `c` (`TreeCircuit.ind`).  A literal: `neg_lit`, then
`eval_lit` and the value of a literal (`Lit.eval`, whose reader is missing; see the census)
with the sign flipped.  A gate `node b cs`: `neg_node`; for `b = true` the negated gate is an
`∨`-gate, so `eval_node_false` gives `(cs.map neg).any (·.eval x)`, which by the induction
hypothesis is `cs.any (! ·.eval x) = !(cs.all (·.eval x))`, that is `!` of `eval_node_true`;
`b = false` is symmetric. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.neg_eval (c : TreeCircuit n) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    c.neg.eval x = !c.eval x := by
  sorry

/-- **F1, depth.** De Morgan negation preserves the depth: `c.neg.depth = c.depth`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `c` (`TreeCircuit.ind`).  A literal stays a literal (depth `0`
on both sides; the reader `depth_lit` is missing, see the census).  A gate: `neg_node` and
`depth_node` reduce the claim to `maxDepth (cs.map neg) = maxDepth cs`, an induction on the
list with `maxDepth_nil`/`maxDepth_cons` and the induction hypothesis on each child. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_neg (c : TreeCircuit n) : c.neg.depth = c.depth := by
  sorry

/-- **F1, fan-in.** De Morgan negation preserves the fan-in: `c.neg.maxFanin = c.maxFanin`.
Glue.

**Proof sketch.** As for `depth_neg`: induction on `c`; a gate keeps its arity
(`List.length_map`), and `maxFanin_node` with `maxFaninL_nil`/`maxFaninL_cons` and the
induction hypothesis gives `maxFaninL (cs.map neg) = maxFaninL cs`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_neg (c : TreeCircuit n) : c.neg.maxFanin = c.maxFanin := by
  sorry

mutual

/-- Substitution of formulas for variables: `c.subst f` replaces every positive literal
`x_i` of `c` by `f i` and every negative literal `¬x_i` by `(f i).neg`, keeping the gates,
`(lit l).subst f = if l.sign then f l.idx else (f l.idx).neg` and
`(node b cs).subst f = node b (cs.map (·.subst f))`.  It computes `c` on the values of the
`f i` (`TreeCircuit.subst_eval`).  Structural recursion over the nested child list, through
the private list helper `substList`.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.subst {m : ℕ} : TreeCircuit n → (Fin n → TreeCircuit m) → TreeCircuit m
  | .lit l, f => if l.sign then f l.idx else (f l.idx).neg
  | .node b cs, f => .node b (substList cs f)

/-- `TreeCircuit.subst` on every member of a child list:
`substList cs f = cs.map (·.subst f)`. -/
private def substList {m : ℕ} :
    List (TreeCircuit n) → (Fin n → TreeCircuit m) → List (TreeCircuit m)
  | [], _ => []
  | c :: cs, f => c.subst f :: substList cs f

end

/-- Substitution into a literal: the positive literal `x_i` becomes `f i` and the negative
literal `¬x_i` becomes `(f i).neg`,
`(TreeCircuit.lit l).subst f = if l.sign then f l.idx else (f l.idx).neg`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.subst_lit {m : ℕ} (l : Lit n) (f : Fin n → TreeCircuit m) :
    (TreeCircuit.lit l).subst f = if l.sign then f l.idx else (f l.idx).neg := rfl

/-- The list helper of `subst` is `List.map`: `substList cs f = cs.map (·.subst f)`. -/
private theorem substList_eq_map {m : ℕ} (f : Fin n → TreeCircuit m) :
    ∀ cs : List (TreeCircuit n), substList cs f = cs.map fun c => c.subst f
  | [] => rfl
  | c :: cs => congrArg (c.subst f :: ·) (substList_eq_map f cs)

/-- Substitution into a gate substitutes into every child:
`(TreeCircuit.node b cs).subst f = TreeCircuit.node b (cs.map fun c => c.subst f)`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.subst_node {m : ℕ} (b : Bool) (cs : List (TreeCircuit n))
    (f : Fin n → TreeCircuit m) :
    (TreeCircuit.node b cs).subst f = TreeCircuit.node b (cs.map fun c => c.subst f) :=
  congrArg (TreeCircuit.node b) (substList_eq_map f cs)

/-- **F2, value.** Substitution computes the formula on the substituted values:
`(c.subst f).eval x = c.eval fun i => (f i).eval x`.  Glue (r3 §H5.7, F2).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `c` (`TreeCircuit.ind`).  A positive literal: `subst_lit`, and
both sides are `(f i).eval x` (`eval_lit` and the literal's value).  A negative literal: the
left side is `(f i).neg.eval x = !(f i).eval x` by `neg_eval`, which is the value of `¬x_i`
under `fun i => (f i).eval x`.  A gate: `subst_node`, then `eval_node_true`/`eval_node_false`
on both sides, `List.all_map`/`List.any_map` and the induction hypothesis on each child. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.subst_eval {m : ℕ} (c : TreeCircuit n) (f : Fin n → TreeCircuit m)
    (x : Fin m → Bool) : (c.subst f).eval x = c.eval fun i => (f i).eval x := by
  sorry

/-- **F2, depth.** Substitution adds at most the depth of the deepest substituted formula:
`(c.subst f).depth ≤ c.depth + Finset.univ.sup fun i => (f i).depth`.  Glue (r3 §H5.7, F2).

*Deviation from r3's sketch:* r3 writes `⨆ i, (f i).depth`; `SupSet ℕ` is not in this file's
(frozen) import closure, so the supremum over the finite index type is the equal
`Finset.univ.sup`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `c`, with `D = Finset.univ.sup fun i => (f i).depth`.  A
literal: the result is `f i` or `(f i).neg`, of depth `(f i).depth ≤ D`
(`depth_neg`, `Finset.le_sup`), and `c.depth = 0`.  A gate: `subst_node` and `depth_node` give
`1 + maxDepth (cs.map (·.subst f))`; each child is bounded by `child.depth + D` (induction
hypothesis) `≤ maxDepth cs + D` (`depth_le_maxDepth`), so the list maximum is too
(`maxDepth_nil`/`maxDepth_cons`), and `depth_node` on `c` closes it. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_subst_le {m : ℕ} (c : TreeCircuit n) (f : Fin n → TreeCircuit m) :
    (c.subst f).depth ≤ c.depth + Finset.univ.sup fun i => (f i).depth := by
  sorry

/-- **F2, fan-in.** Substitution has the fan-in of the formula or of a substituted formula:
`(c.subst f).maxFanin ≤ max c.maxFanin (Finset.univ.sup fun i => (f i).maxFanin)`.  Glue
(r3 §H5.7, F2; r3 names the lemma without a formula, and `⨆` is written `Finset.univ.sup` as
in `depth_subst_le`).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `c` as in `depth_subst_le`.  A literal becomes `f i` or
`(f i).neg`, of fan-in `(f i).maxFanin` (`maxFanin_neg`, `Finset.le_sup`).  A gate keeps its
arity (`subst_node`, `List.length_map`), and `maxFanin_node`, `maxFaninL_cons` and the
induction hypothesis bound the children. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_subst_le {m : ℕ} (c : TreeCircuit n) (f : Fin n → TreeCircuit m) :
    (c.subst f).maxFanin ≤ max c.maxFanin (Finset.univ.sup fun i => (f i).maxFanin) := by
  sorry

/-! ### Constants and the fan-in-2 gadgets (F3) -/

/-- The constant formula with value `b`: the empty gate, `TreeCircuit.const b = node b []`
(an empty `∧` is `true`, an empty `∨` is `false`).  Depth `1`, fan-in `0`.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.const (b : Bool) : TreeCircuit n :=
  .node b []

/-- The constant formula is the empty gate:
`(TreeCircuit.const b : TreeCircuit n) = TreeCircuit.node b []`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.const_eq (b : Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.const b : TreeCircuit n) = TreeCircuit.node b [] := rfl

/-- **F3, constant: value.** The constant formula evaluates to its constant:
`(TreeCircuit.const b).eval x = b`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `const_eq`, then `eval_node_true` (`[].all _ = true`) for `b = true` and
`eval_node_false` (`[].any _ = false`) for `b = false`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.const_eval (b : Bool) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.const b : TreeCircuit n).eval x = b := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, constant: depth.** The constant formula has depth one:
`(TreeCircuit.const b : TreeCircuit n).depth = 1`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `const_eq`, `depth_node` and `maxDepth_nil`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_const (b : Bool) : (TreeCircuit.const b : TreeCircuit n).depth = 1 := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, constant: fan-in.** The constant formula has fan-in zero:
`(TreeCircuit.const b : TreeCircuit n).maxFanin = 0`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `const_eq`, `maxFanin_node`, `List.length_nil` and `maxFaninL_nil`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_const (b : Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.const b : TreeCircuit n).maxFanin = 0 := by
  sorry

/-- The binary conjunction `TreeCircuit.and2 a b = node true [a, b]`.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.and2 (a b : TreeCircuit n) : TreeCircuit n :=
  .node true [a, b]

/-- The binary conjunction is a two-child `∧`-gate:
`TreeCircuit.and2 a b = TreeCircuit.node true [a, b]`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.and2_eq (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    TreeCircuit.and2 a b = TreeCircuit.node true [a, b] := rfl

/-- The binary disjunction `TreeCircuit.or2 a b = node false [a, b]`.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.or2 (a b : TreeCircuit n) : TreeCircuit n :=
  .node false [a, b]

/-- The binary disjunction is a two-child `∨`-gate:
`TreeCircuit.or2 a b = TreeCircuit.node false [a, b]`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.or2_eq (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    TreeCircuit.or2 a b = TreeCircuit.node false [a, b] := rfl

/-- The binary exclusive or `TreeCircuit.xor2 a b = or2 (and2 a b.neg) (and2 a.neg b)`, that
is `(a ∧ ¬b) ∨ (¬a ∧ b)` with the negations by De Morgan (`neg`).  Two levels above its
arguments.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.xor2 (a b : TreeCircuit n) : TreeCircuit n :=
  TreeCircuit.or2 (TreeCircuit.and2 a b.neg) (TreeCircuit.and2 a.neg b)

/-- The exclusive or as a formula:
`TreeCircuit.xor2 a b = TreeCircuit.or2 (TreeCircuit.and2 a b.neg) (TreeCircuit.and2 a.neg b)`.
-/
theorem TreeCircuit.xor2_eq (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    TreeCircuit.xor2 a b = TreeCircuit.or2 (TreeCircuit.and2 a b.neg) (TreeCircuit.and2 a.neg b) :=
  rfl

/-- The three-input exclusive or (the full adder's sum bit)
`TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c = xor2 (xor2 a b) c`.  Four levels above its arguments.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.xor3 (a b c : TreeCircuit n) : TreeCircuit n :=
  TreeCircuit.xor2 (TreeCircuit.xor2 a b) c

/-- The three-input exclusive or as nested binary ones:
`TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c = TreeCircuit.xor2 (TreeCircuit.xor2 a b) c`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.xor3_eq (a b c : TreeCircuit n) :
    TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c = TreeCircuit.xor2 (TreeCircuit.xor2 a b) c := rfl

/-- The three-input majority (the full adder's carry bit)
`TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c = or2 (and2 a b) (and2 c (or2 a b))`, that is
`(a ∧ b) ∨ (c ∧ (a ∨ b))`.  Three levels above its arguments.  Glue. -/
def TreeCircuit.maj3 (a b c : TreeCircuit n) : TreeCircuit n :=
  TreeCircuit.or2 (TreeCircuit.and2 a b) (TreeCircuit.and2 c (TreeCircuit.or2 a b))

/-- The majority as a formula: `TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c =
TreeCircuit.or2 (TreeCircuit.and2 a b) (TreeCircuit.and2 c (TreeCircuit.or2 a b))`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maj3_eq (a b c : TreeCircuit n) :
    TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c =
      TreeCircuit.or2 (TreeCircuit.and2 a b) (TreeCircuit.and2 c (TreeCircuit.or2 a b)) := rfl

/-- **F3, `and2`: value.** `(TreeCircuit.and2 a b).eval x = (a.eval x && b.eval x)`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `and2_eq`, `eval_node_true`, and `List.all_cons`/`List.all_nil`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.and2_eval (a b : TreeCircuit n) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.and2 a b).eval x = (a.eval x && b.eval x) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `and2`: depth `+1`.** `(TreeCircuit.and2 a b).depth ≤ max a.depth b.depth + 1`.
Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `and2_eq`, `depth_node`, `maxDepth_cons` twice and `maxDepth_nil`; then
`omega` (it is an equality). -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_and2_le (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.and2 a b).depth ≤ max a.depth b.depth + 1 := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `and2`: fan-in two.**
`(TreeCircuit.and2 a b).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin b.maxFanin)`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `and2_eq`, `maxFanin_node` (arity `2`), `maxFaninL_cons` twice and
`maxFaninL_nil`; then `omega`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_and2_le (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.and2 a b).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin b.maxFanin) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `or2`: value.** `(TreeCircuit.or2 a b).eval x = (a.eval x || b.eval x)`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `or2_eq`, `eval_node_false`, and `List.any_cons`/`List.any_nil`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.or2_eval (a b : TreeCircuit n) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.or2 a b).eval x = (a.eval x || b.eval x) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `or2`: depth `+1`.** `(TreeCircuit.or2 a b).depth ≤ max a.depth b.depth + 1`.
Glue.

**Proof sketch.** As `depth_and2_le`, through `or2_eq`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_or2_le (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.or2 a b).depth ≤ max a.depth b.depth + 1 := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `or2`: fan-in two.**
`(TreeCircuit.or2 a b).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin b.maxFanin)`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** As `maxFanin_and2_le`, through `or2_eq`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_or2_le (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.or2 a b).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin b.maxFanin) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `xor2`: value.** `(TreeCircuit.xor2 a b).eval x = (a.eval x ^^ b.eval x)`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `xor2_eq`, `or2_eval`, `and2_eval` and `neg_eval`; then a case split on the
two Booleans. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.xor2_eval (a b : TreeCircuit n) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.xor2 a b).eval x = (a.eval x ^^ b.eval x) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `xor2`: depth `+2`.** `(TreeCircuit.xor2 a b).depth ≤ max a.depth b.depth + 2`.
Glue; the constant `2` is settled by the construction (one `∧` level, one `∨` level, and the
depth-preserving `neg`).

**Proof sketch.** `xor2_eq`, `depth_or2_le`, `depth_and2_le` twice, and `depth_neg` for
`a.neg`, `b.neg`; then `omega`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_xor2_le (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.xor2 a b).depth ≤ max a.depth b.depth + 2 := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `xor2`: fan-in two.**
`(TreeCircuit.xor2 a b).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin b.maxFanin)`.  Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `xor2_eq`, `maxFanin_or2_le`, `maxFanin_and2_le` and `maxFanin_neg`; then
`omega`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_xor2_le (a b : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.xor2 a b).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin b.maxFanin) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `xor3`: value** (the full adder's sum bit).
`(TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c).eval x = (a.eval x ^^ b.eval x ^^ c.eval x)`.  Glue (r3 §H5.7, F3).

**Proof sketch.** `xor3_eq` and `xor2_eval` twice. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.xor3_eval (a b c : TreeCircuit n) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c).eval x = (a.eval x ^^ b.eval x ^^ c.eval x) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `xor3`: depth `+4`.**
`(TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c).depth ≤ max a.depth (max b.depth c.depth) + 4`.  Glue; r3's `+4`
*(fix)*, settled by the construction: two nested `xor2`, each `+2`.

**Proof sketch.** `xor3_eq`, `depth_xor2_le` twice; then `omega`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_xor3_le (a b c : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c).depth ≤ max a.depth (max b.depth c.depth) + 4 := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `xor3`: fan-in two.**
`(TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin (max b.maxFanin c.maxFanin))`.
Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `xor3_eq` and `maxFanin_xor2_le` twice; then `omega`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_xor3_le (a b c : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.xor3 a b c).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin (max b.maxFanin c.maxFanin)) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `maj3`: value** (the full adder's carry bit, in the form of `carryBit`'s step).
`(TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c).eval x = (a.eval x && b.eval x || c.eval x && (a.eval x ^^ b.eval x))`.
Glue (r3 §H5.7, F3).  The formula computes `(a ∧ b) ∨ (c ∧ (a ∨ b))`, which is the same
Boolean function.

**Proof sketch.** `maj3_eq`, `or2_eval`, `and2_eval` twice and `or2_eval` again; then a case
split on the three Booleans. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maj3_eval (a b c : TreeCircuit n) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    (TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c).eval x =
      (a.eval x && b.eval x || c.eval x && (a.eval x ^^ b.eval x)) := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `maj3`: depth `+3`.**
`(TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c).depth ≤ max a.depth (max b.depth c.depth) + 3`.  Glue; r3's `+3`
*(fix)*, settled by the construction `(a ∧ b) ∨ (c ∧ (a ∨ b))`.

**Proof sketch.** `maj3_eq`, `depth_or2_le` twice and `depth_and2_le` twice; then `omega`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.depth_maj3_le (a b c : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c).depth ≤ max a.depth (max b.depth c.depth) + 3 := by
  sorry

/-- **F3, `maj3`: fan-in two.**
`(TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin (max b.maxFanin c.maxFanin))`.
Glue.

**Proof sketch.** `maj3_eq`, `maxFanin_or2_le` twice and `maxFanin_and2_le` twice; then
`omega`. -/
theorem TreeCircuit.maxFanin_maj3_le (a b c : TreeCircuit n) :
    (TreeCircuit.maj3 a b c).maxFanin ≤ max 2 (max a.maxFanin (max b.maxFanin c.maxFanin)) := by
  sorry

end BoolCircuit

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/CircuitComplexity/FormulaArith/CarrySave.lean (Lean, at 73aedcdaaaffef7e69ab012d9b9195f150bae68d) =====

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
